# HCodeSnippet

> Copyable code examples with keyboard-accessible language, file, or framework tabs.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.9.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HCodeSnippet` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-code-snippet>`.
- Constructor: `HearthCodeSnippetElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Developer.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HCodeSnippet.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- Options are properties, never JSON attributes. Each option has a stable id, visible label and literal code. Native tab semantics, arrow/Home/End navigation, copy feedback, wrap and bounded scrolling work in both builds. Code is escaped plain text, not a syntax highlighter. copied emits the active option id.

## Public API

options: CodeSnippetOption[] · modelValue: string · label: string · wrap, lineNumbers: boolean · maxHeight: string

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    options: CodeSnippetOption[];
    modelValue?: string;
    label?: string;
    wrap?: boolean;
    lineNumbers?: boolean;
    maxHeight?: string;
};
```

### Defaults

```ts
{ options: () => [], label: "Code examples", maxHeight: "360px" }
```

### Events

update:modelValue(string), change(string), copied(string), copy-error(string)

```ts
type Emits = {
    "update:modelValue": [
        id: string
    ];
    change: [
        id: string
    ];
    copied: [
        id: string
    ];
    "copy-error": [
        message: string
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, empty

Use `hearth-code-snippet::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Supporting types

```ts
export interface CodeSnippetOption {
    id: string;
    label: string;
    code: string;
    language?: string;
    filename?: string;
    disabled?: boolean;
}
```

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HCodeSnippet } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';

</script>

<template>
  <HCodeSnippet label="API request" :options="[{id:'curl',label:'cURL',language:'sh',code:'curl https://api.example.com/status'},{id:'js',label:'JavaScript',language:'js',code:'const response = await fetch(endpoint);'}]" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-code-snippet');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "API request",
  "options": [
    {
      "id": "curl",
      "label": "cURL",
      "language": "sh",
      "code": "curl https://api.example.com/status"
    },
    {
      "id": "js",
      "label": "JavaScript",
      "language": "js",
      "code": "const response = await fetch(\"/status\");"
    }
  ]
});

element.addEventListener('change', event => {
  const [value] = event.detail;
  // Update your application state using value.
});

mount.append(element);
```
